parties.respondent: The Oriental Insurance Company Limited & Anr.

summary: The case involved an insurance claim dispute where the insurer repudiated a claim for theft of a vehicle due to alleged delay in intimation, despite timely FIR registration. The key issue was whether a delay in informing the insurer, while reporting theft to police promptly, justified total repudiation of claim under Condition No. 1 of the policy. The Supreme Court interpreted the insurance contract, emphasizing contra proferentem and the distinction between accidental loss and theft. It held that delay in intimation, without evidence of prejudice to the insurer, cannot lead to denial of claim, particularly when the vehicle remained untraceable. The NCDRC's order setting aside lower forums' decisions was overturned.
legal_provisions_cited: Condition No. 1 of Standard Form for Commercial Vehicles Package Policy
Om Prakash vs. Reliance General Insurance & Another
Oriental Insurance Company Limited vs. Parvesh Chander Chadha
Gurshinder Singh vs. Shriram General Insurance Company Ltd. & Another, 2020 (11) SCC 612
final_judgment: The appeal was allowed. The order of the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission setting aside the State Commission's judgment was quashed. The decision of the State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission was restored, directing the insurance company to pay the insured amount of Rs. 12,79,399/- with interest at 9% p.a. from the date of filing of the complaint till realization, along with compensation of Rs. 10,000/- and litigation expenses of Rs. 5,000/-.
